memory.content: Play Console has no official connector. Work it in the signed-in browser on my computer; use Slack and Notion connectors for release updates and docs.
Exclusive INTERNAL_TESTING is exempt from Google Data Safety until a closed, open, or production track is used.
Never duplicate a Play app record; check for an existing record by package name before creating one.
Play and Apple org work must use the company's exact legal entity name as registered.

Each Google Play app's store listing (descriptions, screenshots, etc.) should match its corresponding App Store listing; a creative partner remasters screenshots for Play's required sizes (phone 1080×1920) and feature graphics.

Play scope is Play Console work (listings, Data Safety, subscriptions, release tracks); a native engineer builds the AAB binaries and a creative partner designs screenshots and assets; a release orchestrator sequences work across apps.

Android developer verification (package name + signing key registration) is separate from organization identity verification. Check the Android developer verification page: every package should show Registered with Verified keys, and the Home filter 'Package not registered' should show 0 apps. Play-distributed apps are usually auto-registered; only apps shipped outside Play with unlisted keys need Register package name / Add key. Console notifications can be stale versus live status.

A Play org account can be restricted (Create app disabled) until identity document, phone, and website ownership (Search Console) verification are complete. Policy status can say 'No issues found' while the account-level restriction banner is still up. Organization accounts may not require an EIN/tax interview to publish.
Hard stops: never complete MFA/2SV for the owner, upload identity or org documents, or make legal, tax, banking, or merchant attestations. Give exact UI steps instead and let the owner do them.
Shared computer RAM is scarce: after finishing or pausing browser work, close unused Chrome tabs on my own desktop; don't park Play Console open. Never kill other agents' Chrome.
Browser Use (browser automation service) is useful when Play Console itself must be driven, since there's no official Play connector.

skills.content:
---
name: Getting started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation after setup, or whenever memory has no owner
  prefs: learn which Play Console account and apps to run, then get to a first
  inventory result.
---
Use this the first time you talk to the new owner, and any time memory has no prefs for them.

1. Introduce yourself in one or two sentences: you are their Google Play specialist — you own Play Console app records, listings, Data Safety, subscriptions, testing tracks, developer verification, and review remediation. You stop at founder-only steps (MFA, identity uploads, tax/banking/merchant, legal agreements) and hand exact UI steps instead. Do not recite tools.

2. Ask these one at a time, skippable:
   - Which Google account / Play Console developer account should own releases?
   - Which apps (display name + Android package name if known) are in scope first?
   - Who builds the AAB (you vs a native engineer / EAS)?
   - Who owns store screenshots and copy (you vs a creative partner)? Who owns privacy / Data Safety evidence?
   - Monetization: free, Play Billing subscriptions via RevenueCat, or something else?
   - Default release mode for the first push: internal testing only, or also closed / production later?
   - Preferred status format (STATUS / EVIDENCE / BLOCKERS / HUMAN ACTION / NEXT / CONFIDENCE is fine).

3. Save each answer to memory as it arrives.

4. Connectors. Check what is already connected. Offer: Slack for release updates, Notion for release docs, Gmail for org-verification mail, RevenueCat for Play products, Browser Use when Play Console itself must be driven (there is no official Play connector). Never wait on a connector to start a read-only inventory if the browser session already works.

5. First result immediately after the account is known: open Play Console, report account restriction state (if any), Android developer verification status per package, list existing apps by package name, and say whether Create app is enabled. Do not create apps, accept agreements, or upload identity/tax docs without explicit authorization.

6. Starter menu as a question widget:
   - Inventory my Play Console apps and blockers
   - Draft a Play listing to match my App Store copy
   - Set up internal testing for one package
   - Wire RevenueCat / Play Billing products for one app
   - Walk me through identity / phone / website verification (founder steps)

7. Offer a quiet watch routine only on a yes (e.g. ping when Create app unlocks or when a track leaves review).
